title: Ignore local temp/ scratch directory
summary: A three-line change to .gitignore that adds a `temp/` entry under a new comment, so local scratch files stop showing up as untracked in git status. Nothing in the build, test or runtime path changes; the only effect is on which working-tree files git considers part of the repository.

lanes.label: Developer working tree
lanes.subtitle: local checkout
lanes.summary: Files a developer creates while working, including the scratch directory this change is about.

lanes.label: Ignore rules
lanes.subtitle: .gitignore
lanes.summary: The pattern file git consults before deciding whether a path is tracked.

lanes.label: Git
lanes.subtitle: index and status
lanes.summary: The tooling that classifies paths and produces the diff a reviewer reads.

nodes.label: temp/
nodes.subtitle: local scratch, never committed
nodes.summary: A developer-local scratch directory. It is not part of the repository and is not produced by any build step; it exists only on the machine of whoever is working.

nodes.label: docs/temp-context/
nodes.subtitle: temporary working context and plans
nodes.summary: An already-ignored directory for temporary working context and implementation plans. It sits directly below the new entry in the file and is the neighbour that shows the convention this change follows.

nodes.label: .gitignore
nodes.subtitle: root ignore rules
nodes.summary: The root ignore file. This change adds a comment line and a `temp/` pattern between the worktree entries and the existing docs/temp-context/ entry.

nodes.label: git status / add
nodes.subtitle: path classification
nodes.summary: The step that walks the working tree and asks the ignore rules whether each path is worth reporting. It is the only consumer of the new pattern.

nodes.label: Git index
nodes.subtitle: staged tree
nodes.summary: The staged snapshot. Because temp/ is now ignored, nothing under it can reach the index by accident.

edges.label: matched by temp/
edges.summary: The new pattern is what makes the scratch directory invisible to git. This is the whole change.

edges.label: matched by docs/temp-context/
edges.summary: The pre-existing sibling rule, unchanged, showing the same convention already in use.

edges.label: pattern list
edges.summary: Git reads the ignore file on every status and add, so the new line takes effect immediately with no build step.

edges.label: staged paths
edges.summary: Only non-ignored paths can be staged, which is the practical consequence of the new rule.

flows.title: How a temp/ file is classified
flows.summary: The path a developer's scratch file takes from creation to being silently skipped by git.

messages.label: developer writes scratch file
messages.note: Nothing in the repository creates this file; it is purely local.

messages.label: temp/ matches
messages.note: Before this change the path fell through to the untracked list; now it is skipped.

messages.label: no path staged
messages.note: The index is untouched, which is the point: scratch work can no longer be committed by accident.

views.title: Ignore rules and their consumers
views.summary: The working tree, the ignore file and the git tooling that reads it. Only the .gitignore node changed; everything else is the context that gives the change its meaning.

views.title: Path classification sequence
views.summary: The ordered path a scratch file takes through git's ignore check.
